soil.title: DIY Soil Test
soil.subtitle: Jar sedimentation test, texture estimation, and rough pH check
soil.honestyNotice: This is an estimate. It does not measure nutrients (NPK). For exact nutrient levels, get a government Soil Health Card lab test.
soil.jarTestTitle: How to Do the Jar Test
soil.jarStep1: Fill about one third (1/3) of a straight-sided clear jar with soil (remove stones and debris).
soil.jarStep2: Fill nearly full with clean water and add a small spoon of dish soap if available (helps particles separate).
soil.jarStep3: Close the lid tightly and shake well for about 3 minutes. Place it on a flat place.
soil.jarStep4: Mark or note the settling times:
soil.sandLayer: Sand (bottom layer): Settles in about 1 minute.
soil.siltLayer: Silt (middle layer): Settles after about 2 hours.
soil.clayLayer: Clay (top layer): Settles after 24 hours or more.
soil.phDesc: Two small checks with kitchen items to check if your soil is acidic or alkaline:
soil.phVinegarDesc: Put a little dry soil in a cup and add vinegar. Fizzing suggests lime-rich, likely alkaline soil (pH > 7.5).
soil.phBakingSodaDesc: In another cup, make a muddy paste with water and add baking soda. Fizzing suggests acidic soil (pH < 6.5).
soil.phNeutral: No fizz in both means roughly neutral soil (pH 6.5 - 7.5), which is ideal for most crops.
soil.phLabNotice: This is a rough test. The Soil Health Card lab test is the accurate way.
soil.helperDrag: Drag the lines to where each layer ends (Sand, Silt, and Total Soil):
soil.soilHealthCardDesc: Get official government laboratory soil testing with customized fertilizer recommendations.
